She also serves as the Board’s legal representative and liaison to the General Counsel and other offices of the Board. Ms. Cocuzza brings to the Board more than two decades of experience in labor law, administrative law, and workplace relations. She began her legal career as an Honors Attorney for then-NLRB General Counsel Ronald Meisburg, gaining experience with various GC-side branches including Regional Advice, Appeals, and Appellate and Supreme Court Litigation, as well as the Region 5 Washington Resident Office. summary: We have seen demands being made for people to repay loans, or purported loans, provided as part of disguised remuneration schemes. Disguised remuneration schemes saw people – often contractors, consultants and agency workers – paid for their work through loans instead of regular salaries as a way to avoid tax. HMRC has sought to tackle this tax avoidance through what has been termed the loan charge and published guidance for those affected.Questions have been raised about the regulatory status of these loans and whether they were ever intended to be repaid.Some of those affected dispute liability for the amounts being claimed and challenge whether the debts can be legally enforced. If they’re unenforceable, borrowers cannot be forced to pay the money back or have any of their assets seized against the debt without a specific order.Some consumers are, however being sent legal letters threatening potential court action and asking for immediate repayment of the loan.
